title: Taiwan Dollar Falls to Weakest Level in 18 Months as Shares Slide
summaryZh: 外資大舉賣股，新台幣跌至一年半新低，央行稱必要時將進場。
summaryHi: विदेशी निवेशकों की बिकवाली से ताइवान डॉलर 18 महीने के निचले स्तर पर पहुँचा।
summaryEs: La venta de acciones por inversores extranjeros hunde el dólar taiwanés a su nivel más bajo en 18 meses.
summaryJa: 外国人投資家の売りで台湾ドルが1年半ぶりの安値に、中央銀行は介入も示唆。
summaryKo: 외국인 투자자의 주식 매도로 대만 달러가 18개월 만에 최저치로 떨어졌다.
summaryEn: Foreign investors are selling Taiwanese shares, and the Taiwan dollar has dropped to its lowest level in 18 months.
paragraphs: The Taiwan dollar has slid to its weakest level in roughly 18 months, as foreign investors continue to pull money out of the island's stock market. On Monday the currency briefly weakened to NT$32.57 against the US dollar, its lowest point since April last year, before recovering slightly to close at NT$32.445.

Foreign institutional investors sold a net NT$76.74 billion (US$2.37 billion) of local shares on Monday alone. That followed a week in which they offloaded US$19.4 billion in Taiwanese equities and sent a net US$17.96 billion abroad, the currency's steepest weekly fall in more than a year.

Analysts link the selling to a worldwide correction in technology stocks. Investors have grown nervous about sky-high valuations of AI-related firms and about whether massive spending on AI infrastructure will ever pay off. Higher oil prices have also raised fears of inflation in the US, which could push the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates high.

Because Taiwan's market is dominated by chipmakers, it has been hit hard: the Taiex fell 4.47 percent last week. Even so, the central bank described it as relatively resilient, noting that the US Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 15.7 percent between October 7 and 16.

In a rare statement issued during trading hours, the central bank said it would monitor capital flows and intervene when necessary to maintain the currency's stability. Several local newspapers reported on Tuesday that government-led funds had also stepped in to support share prices.
Taiwan's money is called the Taiwan dollar. This week, it is getting weaker.
On Monday, one US dollar cost more than 32.5 Taiwan dollars for a short time. This has not happened since April last year.

Why is this happening? Many people from other countries own shares in Taiwanese companies. Now they are selling a lot of them. On Monday alone, they sold shares worth about 2.4 billion US dollars. When they sell, they change their Taiwan dollars back into US dollars and take the money out of Taiwan.
Big technology companies are losing value all over the world. Some people think these companies, especially AI companies, cost too much. Taiwan has many technology companies, so its shares fell too.
Taiwan's central bank says it is watching closely. It says it can act to stop big changes in the money's value.

The Taiwan dollar has fallen to its weakest level in about a year and a half. On Monday it briefly dropped to 32.57 against the US dollar, the lowest point since April last year, before closing at 32.445.

The main reason is that foreign investors are selling Taiwanese shares in large amounts. On Monday they sold about NT$76.7 billion (US$2.37 billion) more than they bought. Last week they sold shares worth US$19.4 billion and moved almost US$18 billion out of the country.

The selling is part of a global fall in technology shares. Many investors are worried that AI companies are too expensive and that huge spending on AI may not pay off. Rising interest rates in the US are also making American investments more attractive.
Taiwan's main share index, the Taiex, lost 4.47 percent last week. The central bank pointed out that a key US chip index fell much more, by 15.7 percent, since early October.

The bank said it is watching the markets and may step in when necessary to keep the currency stable. It made a rare statement during trading hours, and local newspapers said government-backed funds were also buying shares.

The Taiwan dollar has slid to its weakest level in roughly 18 months, as foreign investors continue to pull money out of the island's stock market. On Monday the currency briefly weakened to NT$32.57 against the US dollar, its lowest point since April last year, before recovering slightly to close at NT$32.445.

Foreign institutional investors sold a net NT$76.74 billion (US$2.37 billion) of local shares on Monday alone. That followed a week in which they offloaded US$19.4 billion in Taiwanese equities and sent a net US$17.96 billion abroad, the currency's steepest weekly fall in more than a year.

Analysts link the selling to a worldwide correction in technology stocks. Investors have grown nervous about sky-high valuations of AI-related firms and about whether massive spending on AI infrastructure will ever pay off. Higher oil prices have also raised fears of inflation in the US, which could push the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates high.

Because Taiwan's market is dominated by chipmakers, it has been hit hard: the Taiex fell 4.47 percent last week. Even so, the central bank described it as relatively resilient, noting that the US Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 15.7 percent between October 7 and 16.

In a rare statement issued during trading hours, the central bank said it would monitor capital flows and intervene when necessary to maintain the currency's stability. Several local newspapers reported on Tuesday that government-led funds had also stepped in to support share prices.

The Taiwan dollar has sunk to an 18-month low, dragged down by a sustained exodus of foreign capital from the island's equity market. The currency touched NT$32.57 against the greenback in intraday trading on Monday, a level not seen since April last year, before paring its losses to settle at NT$32.445.

The scale of the selling is striking. Foreign institutions dumped a net NT$76.74 billion (US$2.37 billion) of Taiwanese shares on Monday, on top of US$19.4 billion the previous week, when net outflows reached almost US$18 billion and the currency suffered its sharpest weekly decline in over a year.

The retreat mirrors a broader rout in global technology stocks. Doubts are mounting over whether the vast sums being poured into AI infrastructure will generate adequate returns, while stubbornly high oil prices have revived inflation worries in the US and raised the prospect of a more hawkish Federal Reserve, which meets on October 27 and 28.

Given the heavy weighting of semiconductor firms in the Taiex, the index shed 4.47 percent last week. The central bank, however, argued that the market had held up comparatively well, pointing out that the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had plunged 15.7 percent over the same period.

In an unusual mid-session statement, the bank pledged to keep a close eye on cross-border fund flows and to intervene when warranted to preserve the currency's 'dynamic stability'. Local media also reported that state-backed funds had entered the market to cushion the slide.

The Taiwan dollar has fallen to its lowest value in a year and a half, a development that illustrates how quickly sentiment in global financial markets can shift. On Monday the currency briefly reached NT$32.57 per US dollar, its weakest point since April last year, before ending the day at NT$32.445.

The immediate cause is a large-scale withdrawal of foreign investment. Overseas institutions sold a net US$2.37 billion of Taiwanese shares on Monday, following net sales of US$19.4 billion the previous week. As these investors convert their proceeds into US dollars, demand for the local currency inevitably declines.

This trend reflects wider anxiety about the technology sector. Many investors now question whether the enormous investment in artificial intelligence will deliver sufficient profits, and rising US inflation, partly driven by expensive oil, suggests that interest rates may remain elevated, making dollar assets more appealing.

Taiwan is particularly exposed because semiconductor manufacturers account for a substantial proportion of its stock market. Nevertheless, the central bank emphasised that the Taiex, which dropped 4.47 percent last week, had performed considerably better than a leading US chip index, which fell 15.7 percent.

In a rare announcement during trading hours, the bank stated that it would monitor capital flows closely and intervene if necessary to maintain stability. Whether such measures can restore confidence may depend largely on the US Federal Reserve's decision later this month.

out.ex: The workers held out for more pay.

outflows.en: amounts of money moving out of a place
outflows.ex: Fund outflows rose for the third week.

over.en: take over: get control of a company
over.ex: A new manager took over the hotel last year.

overseas.en: from or in a foreign country
overseas.ex: The school welcomes many overseas students.

part.ex: Teachers will take part in the strike.

per.ex: The ticket costs ten euro per person.

percent.ex: Ten percent of the class was absent.

performed.ex: The new shop performed well in its first year.

period.ex: The museum is closed for a short period.

philadelphia.en: a US city; also a chip stock index

plunged.en: fell suddenly and by a large amount
plunged.ex: Oil prices plunged after the news.

pointed.ex: He pointed to the rise in sales.

pointing.ex: She explained her view, pointing to recent data.

poured.en: put in large amounts of money
poured.ex: Billions have been poured into new roads.

preserve.ex: We must preserve these old photos.

previous.ex: The previous owner lived here for years.

prices.ex: The price of bread has gone up.

profits.en: money a business makes after costs
profits.ex: The company's profits rose sharply this year.

proportion.ex: A large proportion of food is imported.

prospect.en: the idea of a possible future event
prospect.ex: The prospect of moving abroad scared her.

pull.en: (pull together) work together as a team
pull.ex: If we all pull together, we can finish today.

push.en: push back: move to a later time
push.ex: Bad weather may push the launch back a week.

question.ex: Many people question whether the plan will work.

rare.ex: It is rare to see snow in this city.

rates.en: levels measured as amounts or percentages

reached.ex: They reached an agreement at midnight.

reason.ex: There is no reason to worry.

recovering.en: getting back to a better level
recovering.ex: Prices are slowly recovering after last month's drop.

reflects.en: shows or is caused by something

relatively.ex: The test was relatively easy for most students.

remain.ex: Most visitors remain in the city centre.

reported.ex: The theft was reported to the police.

reserve.en: part of 'Federal Reserve', the US central bank
reserve.ex: The Federal Reserve sets interest rates in the US.

reserve's.ex: The Reserve's decision surprised many investors.

resilient.ex: Local shops proved resilient during the crisis.

example.en: Tourism has proved resilient despite rising prices.
example.zh: 儘管物價上漲，旅遊業仍展現出韌性。

note.meaning: 有韌性的、能承受困難並迅速恢復的；（信心、經濟）保持穩健。
note.usage: 常用 remain/prove resilient；可形容人、經濟、市場、需求等。名詞為 resilience。

noteHi.exampleTr: बढ़ती कीमतों के बावजूद पर्यटन मज़बूत बना रहा।
noteHi.meaning: कठिनाई के बाद भी मज़बूत रहने वाला।
noteHi.usage: remain/prove resilient के साथ आम; संज्ञा resilience।

noteEs.exampleTr: El turismo se ha mostrado resiliente pese a la subida de precios.
noteEs.meaning: que resiste las dificultades y se mantiene firme.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con remain/prove resilient; sustantivo: resilience.

noteJa.exampleTr: 物価上昇にもかかわらず観光業は底堅さを示した。
noteJa.meaning: 困難に負けずに持ちこたえる、底堅い。
noteJa.usage: remain/prove resilient の形が多い。名詞は resilience。

noteKo.usage: remain/prove resilient 형태로 자주 쓰임. 명사는 resilience.

noteEn.meaning: able to stay strong or recover quickly after problems.
noteEn.usage: Often 'remain resilient' or 'prove resilient'; the noun is 'resilience'.

restore.en: repair something so it is like new
restore.ex: They plan to restore the old theatre.

returns.ex: Investors expect good returns from the new fund.

revived.ex: The old festival was revived after twenty years.

rout.en: a sudden heavy fall or defeat
rout.ex: The market rout wiped out months of gains.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

scale.en: how big or serious something is
scale.ex: Nobody expected the scale of the damage.

sector.ex: The public sector employs many people.

seen.ex: I have never seen such a big dog.

sell.ex: They want to sell their car.

selling.ex: The shop started selling coffee last year.

semiconductor.en: material used to make computer chips
semiconductor.ex: Taiwan has a large semiconductor industry.

sent.ex: I sent the form to the office yesterday.

example.en: Bad news quickly hurt market sentiment.
example.zh: 壞消息很快打擊了市場情緒。

noteEn.meaning: the general feeling or opinion of a group of people.

noteHi.exampleTr: बुरी ख़बर ने बाज़ार की धारणा को जल्दी नुकसान पहुँचाया।
noteHi.meaning: लोगों की सामान्य भावना या राय।

noteEs.exampleTr: Las malas noticias dañaron rápido el sentimiento del mercado.
noteEs.meaning: sentimiento u opinión general de un grupo.

noteJa.exampleTr: 悪いニュースで市場心理がすぐに悪化した。
noteJa.meaning: 人々や市場の全体的な気分や見方。

noteKo.exampleTr: 나쁜 소식이 시장 심리를 빠르게 악화시켰다.

settle.en: to end at a level after changes
settle.ex: Oil prices settled slightly higher on Friday.

share.ex: We should share the benefits fairly.

shares.ex: Smaller shares go to other groups.

sharpest.ex: Sales saw their sharpest fall in ten years.

shed.ex: The index shed two percent in early trading.

shift.en: a change in position or view
shift.ex: There was a shift in public opinion.

short.ex: The team fell short of its goal.

sky-high.ex: Sky-high rents are pushing young people out of the city.

slid.ex: The share price slid by five per cent.

slide.ex: The government tried to stop the slide in prices.

so.en: used in 'so far' meaning until now
so.ex: So far, everything is going well.

some.ex: Some fifty people came to the meeting.

stability.en: the state of not changing suddenly
stability.ex: The bank wants to keep price stability.

example.en: Investors want political and economic stability.
example.zh: 投資人希望政治與經濟穩定。

note.usage: 常見 maintain/ensure stability；financial/economic stability；形容詞 stable。

noteEn.meaning: the state of being steady and not changing suddenly.

noteHi.exampleTr: निवेशक राजनीतिक और आर्थिक स्थिरता चाहते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: स्थिरता; अचानक न बदलने की अवस्था।
noteHi.usage: maintain stability; financial stability आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteEs.exampleTr: Los inversores quieren estabilidad política y económica.
noteEs.meaning: estabilidad; estado de no cambiar de repente.
noteEs.usage: Se usa maintain stability; financial stability.

noteJa.exampleTr: 投資家は政治と経済の安定を求めている。
noteJa.meaning: 安定；急に変わらない状態。
noteJa.usage: maintain stability、financial stability の形が多い。

noteKo.usage: maintain stability, financial stability 형태가 흔하다.

stable.ex: A stable job helps people plan their future.

state-backed.en: supported or paid for by the government
state-backed.ex: A state-backed bank lent the money.
state-backed.zh: 國家支持的；政府資助的

stated.ex: The report stated the facts clearly.

statement.ex: The club released a statement this morning.

steepest.en: largest or sharpest (of a rise or change)
steepest.ex: This is the steepest price rise in years.

step.ex: The first step is to fill in the form.

stepped.ex: The city stepped in to save the old theatre.

stock.en: goods that a business has available
stock.ex: The shop has no more stock of this phone.

stocks.ex: Tech stocks fell sharply on Monday.

striking.ex: There is a striking difference between the twins.

stubbornly.ja: 頑固に；なかなか下がらず
stubbornly.en: in a way that is hard to change
stubbornly.ex: Prices have stayed stubbornly high all year.

example.en: Rent takes a substantial part of my salary.
example.zh: 房租占了我薪水的一大部分。

note.usage: 常見 a substantial amount/number/proportion of；比 big 正式，寫作常用。

noteEn.meaning: large in amount, size or importance.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'a substantial amount/proportion of'; more formal than 'big'.

noteHi.exampleTr: किराया मेरी तनख्वाह का बड़ा हिस्सा ले लेता है।
noteHi.meaning: मात्रा या महत्व में काफ़ी बड़ा।
noteHi.usage: a substantial amount/proportion of आम प्रयोग है।

noteEs.exampleTr: El alquiler se lleva una parte considerable de mi sueldo.
noteEs.meaning: considerable; grande en cantidad o importancia.
noteEs.usage: Se usa a substantial amount/proportion of; más formal que big.

noteJa.exampleTr: 家賃が給料のかなりの部分を占めている。
noteJa.usage: a substantial amount/proportion of の形が多い。big より硬い。

noteKo.usage: a substantial amount/proportion of 형태가 흔하다.

sufficient.ex: We have sufficient food for the trip.

suggests.en: shows that something is probably true
suggests.ex: The data suggests people are buying less.

sums.ex: He spent large sums on his car.

sunk.ex: Confidence has sunk to a new low.

support.ja: 支援（support staff：支援スタッフ）

sustained.ex: The city saw a sustained rise in tourism.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

take.ex: Many parents will take a day off.

technology.en: machines and science used in practice

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

think.ex: Experts think a deal is possible.

time.ex: For the first time, dentists will join.

too.ex: The coffee is too hot to drink.

top.ex: Those at the top earn the most.

touched.ex: Gold prices touched a new record on Tuesday.

trading.en: being bought and sold at a certain price
trading.ex: Gold is trading at a high price.

trend.en: a general change or popular fashion
trend.ex: Working from home is a growing trend.

tuesday.ex: The meeting is on Tuesday morning.

unusual.ex: It is unusual for the bank to speak during trading.

valuations.en: estimates of what something is worth
valuations.ex: High valuations worry some careful investors.

value.en: how much money something is worth
value.ex: The value of the house has doubled.

warranted.ex: The bank will act if action is warranted.

watching.ex: Police are watching the area closely.

weakened.ex: The pound weakened against the euro yesterday.

weaker.ex: The yen is weaker than it was a year ago.

weakest.ex: The currency is at its weakest level in years.

weighting.en: the importance given to one part
weighting.ex: Tech firms have a large weighting in the index.

well.ex: She speaks Irish as well as English.

were.ex: The shops were closed on Sunday.

whether.en: used to express a choice (if or not)

wider.ex: The benefits should reach the wider city.

will.en: used to talk about the future
will.ex: The new bridge will open next year.

withdrawal.ex: There was a withdrawal of support.

example.en: The country's withdrawal from the treaty surprised everyone.
example.zh: 該國退出條約令所有人吃驚。

note.usage: a withdrawal from + 組織/協議；動詞 withdraw。

noteHi.exampleTr: देश के संधि से हटने से सभी हैरान हुए।
noteHi.usage: a withdrawal from + संगठन; क्रिया withdraw।

noteEs.exampleTr: La retirada del país del tratado sorprendió a todos.
noteEs.usage: a withdrawal from + organización; verbo: withdraw.

noteJa.meaning: 何かから離脱・撤退すること。
noteJa.exampleTr: その国の条約からの離脱は皆を驚かせた。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 나라의 조약 탈퇴는 모두를 놀라게 했다.

noteEn.meaning: the act of leaving or pulling out of something.
noteEn.usage: Use 'withdrawal from' an organisation; the verb is 'withdraw'.

world.en: the earth and all its countries
world.ex: She wants to travel around the world.

worried.ex: She is worried about her exam.

worries.ex: Money is one of his biggest worries.

worth.ex: The painting is worth a lot of money.

would.ex: A new park would help the town.
